name: Core outcome sets and quality tools
desc: Delphi consensus studies that set core outcome sets and measurement standards (COSMIN), and tools to rate the quality and risk of bias of studies, mostly in medicine.

name: Open science and open access
desc: Open science in general: open access, open research culture, citizen science, and policies for and surveys of open practices across fields.

name: Mixed metascience topics
desc: A broad group without one shared subject: misconduct and retractions, bibliometric methods, p-values and Bayes factors, and research integrity.

name: Reporting guidelines (PRISMA, TRIPOD)
desc: Reporting guidelines and their extensions, such as PRISMA for systematic reviews, TRIPOD for prediction models and STARD for diagnostic accuracy studies.

name: Preregistration and trial registration
desc: Registering studies before they are done: clinical trial registries, preregistration in psychology and qualitative research, and whether registered outcomes match published ones.

name: Journals, preprints and science news
desc: How research is published and reported: journal practices, predatory journals, preprints, publishing during COVID-19, gender gaps among authors, and science journalism.

name: Research ethics and ethics review
desc: The ethics of doing research: ethics committees and review, informed consent, codes of conduct, and ethical questions in health, genomics, neuroscience and online research.

name: FAIR data principles
desc: Making research data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR): what the principles mean, how to measure them, data stewardship and the European Open Science Cloud.

name: Replicability and the replication crisis
desc: Papers about replication itself: the replication crisis, large replication projects, how to judge a replication, and computational reproducibility across fields.

name: Data sharing and data management
desc: Sharing and reusing research data: barriers and motives, data management plans, repositories, and the privacy and governance of health data.

name: Hypothesis testing and statistical evidence
desc: How to test hypotheses and weigh evidence: p-values and significance, Bayes factors, equivalence tests, choosing the alpha level, and planning sample sizes.

name: Clinical and brain research methods
desc: Methods papers within medicine, neuroscience and genetics: replication of genetic associations, reproducibility of neuroimaging, and measurement and bias in depression, pain and brain stimulation research.

name: Statistical methods and meta-analysis
desc: Statistical techniques and tutorials: meta-analysis and corrections for publication bias, sample sizes for prediction models, sequential designs, Bayesian model comparison, and many-analyst studies.

name: Research assessment, integrity and policy
desc: Science policy and research culture: how researchers are assessed and rewarded, research integrity and questionable practices, research funding, and the link between science and policy.

name: Research practices and theory in psychology
desc: Critiques of how psychological research is done: questionable research practices, researcher degrees of freedom, preregistration, measurement and theory building.

name: Peer review
desc: Peer review of papers and grant proposals: its quality, speed and biases, open peer review, registered reports, and the work of editors and reviewers.

name: Replications of specific findings
desc: Replication studies themselves: direct, conceptual and registered replications of particular findings, mostly in psychology and the behavioural sciences.

name: Bibliometrics and citation indicators
desc: Measuring science with publications and citations: impact indicators, the h-index, altmetrics, bibliographic databases and maps of science.

name: Reporting quality in clinical research
desc: Meta-research on published trials and systematic reviews: reporting quality, adherence to guidelines, publication bias, selective outcome reporting and spin.

name: AI and software tools in research
desc: Artificial intelligence and software in research: language models in writing and peer review, machine learning to screen literature for systematic reviews, and research software and metadata.
